A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Infrastructure for AI Agents and provide readable text, four figures, and two tables. Both end with references and contain no appendices. The retained framework and corresponding sections support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 presents a conceptual research agenda with hypothetical examples and schematic figures. Empirical findings are attributed to other work; no original experimental or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains a conceptual research agenda. Its added prioritization discussion and literature-derived examples do not report original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data analyses.

M1.justification: The nine infrastructure concepts and their operating definitions are retained. V2 elaborates existing technical options without introducing a new algorithm, model, or changed agent procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates agents on datasets. Added examples involving voice calls, communication protocols, and blockchain transactions are illustrative applications, not tested task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed implementation. Newly discussed alternatives, including A2A, are literature examples rather than evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an experimental evaluation protocol, data splits, evaluation metrics, sample sizes, or training budgets. New deployment considerations do not constitute experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither presents ablations, robustness experiments, or systematic empirical case analyses. The company example in Section 2.2 remains hypothetical; added limitations are conceptual arguments.

E5.justification: Neither reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical estimation procedures for this work. V2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 newly summarizes qualitative outcomes from cited studies, including language models detecting real-code vulnerabilities in Section 4.2 and emotional cues affecting performance in Section 4.4. These are literature-derived findings, not original infrastructure evaluations or comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither contains mathematical theorems, proofs, or formal derivations. The infrastructure definitions remain substantively unchanged; new prioritization and incentive arguments are informal.

C1.justification: The central thesis, three infrastructure functions, and nine research directions remain unchanged. V2's abstract describes an incomplete catalog, consistent with the non-exhaustiveness already stated in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: New Section 2.3 develops prioritization considerations based on adoption dependencies, capabilities, and threat models. Sections 4.2–4.4 substantially expand oversight-cost tradeoffs, commercial incentives, and blockchain limitations, replacing the earlier low-cost commitment-adoption argument. Section 5.2 adds rollback moral hazard and insurance responses, while Section 6.1 develops adoption barriers. Together these substantially qualify the practical guidance.

D1.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 add technical explanations of HTTP-based A2A communication, negotiated structured formats, and smart-contract deployment and verification. V2 also removes reference URLs to specifications, documentation, and code repositories. These change documented technical and access information; neither version releases an implementation of its infrastructure catalog.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds historical grounding through Kahn and Cerf and Poslad, clarifying how the agenda extends earlier agent protocols. V2 also adds recent work such as Hammond et al. and A2A, while removing the GLEIF reference. The broader positioning within agent governance remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory motivation are rewritten, selected subsections receive expanded explanations, and Sections 2.3 and 6.1 are added. Section 6 is reorganized, with the earlier oversight-usability warning incorporated into Section 4.2. The overall catalog structure and conclusion remain stable.

P2.justification: All four figures and both tables are retained. Figure 3 makes inter-agent communication links bidirectional and reverses the behaviour–oversight arrow. Figures 1 and 2 move relative to surrounding text; publication headers and a more compact reference format also change the layout.

improvement.justification: V1 already provides the core catalog and substantial limitations. V2 improves its practical usefulness through prioritization considerations, clearer connections to existing technologies, and specific qualifications concerning oversight costs, blockchain applicability, and rollback moral hazard. These gains outweigh the reduced source traceability caused by removing reference URLs. Explicit prioritization remains deferred, and the central contribution is unchanged.
